notes: Extra fields beyond SCHEMA.md: match.variant (catalogue variant; '*' is a glob, null matches any) and preferred. Linux recipes were run on Ubuntu 24.04 amd64 in a scratch folder; Windows and macOS are research-only (the 7z listings were read from copies downloaded to scratch).

steps.run: R="{runtime_dir}"; V=$(ls "$R/lib/ruby" | grep -E '^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1); A=$(ls "$R/lib/ruby/$V" | grep -E -- '-linux|-darwin' | head -1); mv "$R/bin/ruby" "$R/bin/ruby.bin"; printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/sh' 'd=$(dirname -- "$(readlink -f -- "$0")"); r=$(dirname -- "$d")' "V=$V; A=$A" 'LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$r/lib${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:+:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH}"' '[ -d "$r/openssl/lib" ] && LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$r/openssl/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH"' 'RUBYLIB="$r/lib/ruby/$V:$r/lib/ruby/$V/$A${RUBYLIB:+:$RUBYLIB}"' 'if [ -d "$r/openssl/ssl" ] && [ -z "$SSL_CERT_FILE" ]; then for f in /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt /etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt /etc/ssl/cert.pem; do [ -f "$f" ] && SSL_CERT_FILE="$f" && break; done; fi' 'export LD_LIBRARY_PATH RUBYLIB SSL_CERT_FILE' 'exec "$d/ruby.bin" "$@"' > "$R/bin/ruby"; chmod 755 "$R/bin/ruby"

'; tail -n +2 "$f"; } > "$f.tmp" && chmod 755 "$f.tmp" && mv "$f.tmp" "$f"; done

prerequisites: glibc >= 2.38 for the ubuntu-24.04 and ubuntu-26.04 builds (highest GLIBC_ symbol version in bin/ruby, libruby and the ext .so files, measured for 2.7.8-ubuntu-24.04, 3.4.10-ubuntu-24.04 and 3.4.10-ubuntu-26.04)

System shared libraries at these sonames: libz.so.1, libgmp.so.10, libffi.so.8, libyaml-0.so.2, libcrypt.so.1 (24.04 builds), libgcc_s.so.1; for 3.x also libssl.so.3/libcrypto.so.3 (the ubuntu-26.04 openssl.so needs symbol version OPENSSL_3.4.0, i.e. OpenSSL >= 3.4); 2.7.8 bundles its own OpenSSL 1.1.1w under openssl/ and also needs libreadline.so.8 and libgdbm.so.6
gcc/make only if the app installs gems with native extensions
recipes.min_os: The Ubuntu release named in the variant, or a distro with the same or newer glibc and library sonames. ubuntu-26.04 builds effectively need a 2026-era distro (OpenSSL >= 3.4).
recipes.notes: ruby-builder tarballs are the setup-ruby GitHub Actions toolcache builds, and they are NOT relocatable as shipped: RUNPATH=/opt/hostedtoolcache/Ruby/<ver>/x64/lib (plus x64/openssl/lib on 2.7), the load path is compiled in (not --enable-load-relative), and bin/gem, bundle, rake etc. have `#!/opt/hostedtoolcache/Ruby/<ver>/x64/bin/ruby`. Unpacked elsewhere, bin/ruby fails with 'libruby.so.X.Y: cannot open shared object file'. The fix steps replace bin/ruby with a sh wrapper (the real binary becomes bin/ruby.bin) that sets LD_LIBRARY_PATH to {runtime_dir}/lib (and openssl/lib), and RUBYLIB to lib/ruby/<ver> and its arch dir. rbconfig.rb then computes TOPDIR from its own location, so RbConfig prefix, Gem.dir and RbConfig.ruby all point into {runtime_dir}. The shebangs of bin/* become the same /bin/sh + `ruby -x` stub that `--enable-load-relative` installs use. TESTED on Ubuntu 24.04 amd64: 3.4.10-ubuntu-24.04 unpacked into '.../app one/rt' and '.../app two/rt' (spaces). After the fix: openssl, psych and zlib loaded, `gem install rainbow` stayed in app one (app two couldn't require it), `gem install bcrypt` compiled its native extension in the path with spaces, and `bundle --version` worked. 2.7.8-ubuntu-24.04 (the plan's file) also worked. Its bundled OpenSSL has OPENSSLDIR under /opt/hostedtoolcache, so without SSL_CERT_FILE, HTTPS verification failed; the wrapper sets it, and after that an HTTPS GET to rubygems.org returned 200. The plan's 3.4.10-ubuntu-26.04 build started on 24.04, but `require 'openssl'` failed (libcrypto.so.3 lacks OPENSSL_3.4.0). Caveats found: (1) executables that gems install later get `#!"{runtime_dir}/bin/ruby"` with quotes, and when the path has a space Linux can't run them directly. `"{runtime_dir}/bin/ruby" "{runtime_dir}/bin/<tool>"` worked. `ruby -S` doesn't, because bin isn't on PATH. (2) The wrapper's environment is inherited by child processes. (3) Only amd64 was run; arm64 tarballs have the same layout. Alternative with no wrapper: build from the source tarball with --enable-load-relative (see the source recipe), which gives RUNPATH ${ORIGIN}/../lib and relative load paths.

recipes.notes: TESTED with ruby-3.4.10.tar.gz (from releases.json; not in the majors plan) on Ubuntu 24.04. With --enable-load-relative, RUNPATH is ${ORIGIN}/../lib and bin/gem etc. get a relative /bin/sh + `ruby -x` stub. Two copies in '.../app one/rt' and '.../app two/rt' each reported their own prefix and Gem.dir, and openssl loaded against system OpenSSL 3. psych was NOT built because libyaml-dev wasn't installed here, and so `gem install` failed ('cannot load such file -- psych'). libyaml-dev is required. Built into a space-free temp prefix and copied, like Python (not tried with a spaced --prefix). The result links the build host's libssl/libyaml/libffi sonames, so build on the oldest target distro.

prerequisites: Homebrew packages gmp, openssl@3 and libyaml at /opt/homebrew/opt/... (arm64) or /usr/local/opt/... (x64): the binaries link them by absolute path
install_name_tool/otool (Xcode Command Line Tools) for the rewrite step
RUBYLIB set as in the Linux wrapper (lib/ruby/<ver> and its arch dir), because the load path is compiled in as /Users/runner/hostedtoolcache/Ruby/<ver>/<arch>
side_effects: Depends on Homebrew-installed gmp/openssl@3/libyaml outside {runtime_dir}, which are shared, upgraded by `brew upgrade`, and absent on most machines
recipes.min_os: The macOS of the GitHub runner that built it (macos-arm64: Apple Silicon; the exact minimum wasn't read from LC_BUILD_VERSION)
recipes.notes: Checked the 3.4.10 darwin-arm64 tarball read-only: rbconfig prefix is /Users/runner/hostedtoolcache/Ruby/3.4.10/arm64. 98 bundles link /Users/runner/hostedtoolcache/.../lib/libruby.3.4.dylib, and bin/ruby, gmp, openssl and psych link /opt/homebrew/opt/{gmp,openssl@3,libyaml}. The binaries are code-signed, so any rewrite needs an ad-hoc re-sign on arm64. The rewrite step is an untested sketch, and a sh wrapper setting RUBYLIB (as on Linux; DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH also works, since SIP only strips DYLD_* when a protected binary is exec'd) is still needed. To reach isolation 'full', copy those three Homebrew dylibs into {runtime_dir}/lib and point the rewritten paths at them. That's the operator's call, because it means shipping Homebrew builds. A cleaner option is building from source with --enable-load-relative and --with-openssl-dir pointing to a private OpenSSL (needs Xcode CLT).

prerequisites: Windows 7 or later (the RubyInstaller2 installer has MinVersion=6.1); arm64 builds need Windows 11 on ARM
Universal C Runtime on Windows 7/8/8.1 for the UCRT builds (Ruby 3.1+: x64-ucrt-ruby*.dll); built into Windows 10+

For gems with C extensions: a private MSYS2 in {runtime_dir}\msys64 (see the devkit recipe, or unpack an msys2-base archive there and run `"{runtime_dir}\bin\ridk.cmd" install 2 3`, which needs network)
recipes.min_os: Windows 7 (x86/x64); Windows 11 ARM64 for -arm builds; Ruby 4.0 has no x86 build
recipes.notes: Listed the 3.4.10 x64 7z (in scratch, not the catalogue): one top folder rubyinstaller-3.4.10-1-x64\ with bin (ruby.exe, x64-ucrt-ruby340.dll, ruby_builtin_dlls), lib, include, share, packages and ridk_use. So strip_components 1. The bin\*.bat/*.cmd launchers call `"%~dp0ruby.exe"` and are relative. The RubyInstaller FAQ says both the exe and the 7z are suitable for portable use. The 7z writes nothing outside the folder: no PATH, no .rb association, no Start-menu entry, no registry. CA certificates: the installer adds a `ssl` junction, but the 7z doesn't need it, because OpenSSL finds the bundled cert.pem at lib\ruby\<ver>\etc\ssl (3.4+), bin\etc\ssl (3.2-3.3) or ssl (<=3.1) (README-SSL.md). Spaces: RubyInstaller advises against paths with spaces or non-ASCII, because some gems won't install, and on <=3.0 ridk won't run at all. So choose a space-free {runtime_dir} on Windows if gems are compiled. MSYS2 lookup (msys2_installation.rb) order: MSYS2_PATH env, {runtime_dir}\msys64, {runtime_dir}\msys32, <parent of runtime_dir>\msys64, then C:\msys64, C:\msys32, the MSYS2 uninstall registry entries, PATH and scoop. So a private {runtime_dir}\msys64 always wins, but without one a machine-wide C:\msys64 is picked up (leak in).

prerequisites: For C extensions: the matching RubyInstaller DevKit (1.9.3: DevKit-tdm-32-4.5.2 self-extracting 7z, not in the catalogue) unpacked into {runtime_dir}\devkit, then `"{runtime_dir}\bin\ruby.exe" "{runtime_dir}\devkit\dk.rb" init` and `... dk.rb install` run from the devkit folder
recipes.notes: Listed ruby-1.9.3-p551-i386-mingw32.7z: one top folder with bin\ruby.exe, msvcrt-ruby191.dll and bundled OpenSSL/zlib/yaml/tcl DLLs, and lib\ruby. bin\gem.bat uses `"%~dp0ruby.exe"` (relative). Runs on XP, which none of the RubyInstaller2 builds do. dk.rb install writes a config.yml holding the absolute ruby path and adds devkit.rb into this ruby's site_ruby/operating_system.rb (private), so re-run it after a move. Its bundled OpenSSL 1.0.x has no current CA bundle, so rubygems.org over HTTPS fails: set SSL_CERT_FILE to a current cacert.pem, or install gems from local .gem files.

steps.run: for /f "tokens=2,*" %A in ('reg query "HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\RubyInstaller-X.Y-ARCH_is1" /v InstallLocation 2^>nul ^| find "InstallLocation"') do if /i "%B"=="{runtime_dir}\" reg delete "HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\RubyInstaller-X.Y-ARCH_is1" /f

prerequisites: Windows 7+ for the installer; the bundled MSYS2 toolchain itself needs a Windows version MSYS2 still supports (Windows 10+ for recent builds)
Replace X.Y/ARCH in the registry step with the installer's AppId parts (e.g. RubyInstaller-3.4-x64; -x86, -arm)
side_effects: Start-menu shortcut {autoprograms}\Ruby X.Y (unconditional in the .iss; there's no AllowNoIcons, so /NOICONS can't suppress it). It's shared by every RubyInstaller X.Y on the machine and points at the last one installed
Programs and Features key HKLM\...\Uninstall\RubyInstaller-X.Y-ARCH_is1 until step 2 removes it (only when its InstallLocation is this {runtime_dir})
If the user already has their own RubyInstaller X.Y (same AppId), this install takes over its Programs and Features entry
recipes.notes: The devkit .exe is the only catalogue file that ships MSYS2 (the compiler toolchain for native gems). It's Inno Setup: 'Inno Setup Setup Data (6.7.0)' in the 3.4.10-1 x64 installer. Its [Setup] has AppId=RubyInstaller-<X.Y>-<arch> (per major.minor, not per patch), PrivilegesRequired=lowest with a command-line override, ChangesEnvironment/ChangesAssociations, and tasks modpath/assocfiles/ridkinstall (all turned off above). [Run] only runs icacls on {app} and {app}\msys64\tmp and makes the `ssl` junction, all inside {runtime_dir}. Two copies of the same X.Y: files install fine to each /dir, but the uninstall key and Start-menu shortcut are shared. Step 2 removes the key only if it belongs to this copy (the cmd `for /f` is written for the command line; double the % signs in a .bat). The Start-menu shortcut is left behind: deleting it risks removing a user's own RubyInstaller shortcut. Safer alternative, pending the operator: take MSYS2 out of the exe without running it. innoextract 1.9 (2020) predates Inno 6.7 data, so it needs a newer innoextract (support unverified). Or use the 7z recipe plus an MSYS2 base archive (msys2.org) unpacked into {runtime_dir}\msys64 and `ridk install 2 3` (network, pacman).
